Position Record

Every position I hold, the reasoning as it stood when I opened it, and the record before it.

Open

GBP/CHF Long FX cross · opened 2026-09-08 -0.16R
  • Sterling yields more than any other currency in the G10 and the franc yields least. CMC passes 2.78% a year of that gap through to a long, so the position earns something while it waits.
  • The risk is a rush into francs. That happens quickly when something goes wrong in Europe, and a stop 1% away does not survive a gap.
Entry1.09592 Stop1.08500 Target1.11650 (1.9R) Last1.09417 Carry+2.78%/yr received
0.84R left to the stop
Japan 225 Long Index · opened 2026-09-08 -0.63R
  • A continuation trade on an index that had been trending, with the stop 3.5% below the entry so it sits outside the index's own daily range.
  • It fell as soon as I was in it and has stayed near the stop since, so the setup I entered on has not done what it was supposed to.
  • The Nikkei usually rallies when the yen is weakening, and I hold this in Australian dollars, so the currency hands back part of any gain in the index.
Entry66,333 Stop64,043 Target70,970 (2.0R) Last64,890 Carry-3.48%/yr charged

USD/MXN Short FX, emerging · opened 2026-09-08 +0.32R
  • Short the dollar against the peso to collect the gap between Banxico and the Fed, which is worth 1.57% a year to me after CMC takes its cut.
  • Financing is the cheapest of anything I hold. CMC charges 1.28% either side of the true rate here, against 8.24% on natural gas.
  • The peso does not drift against you, it gaps. A stop is not much protection in that, so what actually limits the loss is how small the position is.
Entry16.94992 Stop17.14000 Target16.48000 (2.5R) Last16.88900 Carry+1.57%/yr received

Before this page

I traded this account for fourteen months before I started writing the reasoning down. It lost 74% of what I put into it. Here is where the money went, because the answer is not the one I expected.

Paid in, 16 deposits
A$9,175.90
Taken back out
-A$2,844.40
Net in
A$6,331.50
Balance today
A$1,641.00
Result
-A$4,690.50

56% of that loss never went to the market. It went to the broker.

Commission, 205 charges
-A$2,405.25
Holding costs, 1520 daily charges
-A$220.65
Market data
-A$22.00
Total cost
-A$2,647.90

Every dollar of that commission was on share CFDs. CMC charges none on currencies, indices or commodities, so the split is not close: A$2,405.25 against A$0.00. My median hold over that period was 4 days, so I was paying around A$23.47 in commission to hold a share for 4 days in an account this size. No edge survives that, and it is not a question of whether the trades were any good. Everything I hold now is priced by spread and financing instead, which is why the carry number sits on every position above.

The 125 trades below are what I could pair from the statements between 2025-07-07 and 2026-08-22. 29% of them made money. They do not add up to the result at the top: they miss positions that opened or closed outside the statement windows, and they exclude every cost in the table above. The account figure is what actually happened. This is a partial view of how.

R is blank on 67 of these because no stop was recorded when the position opened, and a stop set later is a trailing stop rather than the risk I had accepted. Across the 58 that do carry one the mean is -0.42R. The account reached A$6,127.16 on 2025-10-10 and hit zero on 2025-08-18 and 2025-11-11.

1R is the distance from the entry to the stop I set when I opened the position, so it is the loss I had accepted before I knew the answer. Everything here is quoted in multiples of it, which makes a peso position and an index position comparable and means the page discloses no position sizes. Prices are the market mid as at 2026-09-09, not my broker's fill. Not investment advice.
